newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines probes kidnappings in top school.
newsitem.headline: Philippines probes kidnappings in top school.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday ordered an investigation into the reported kidnapping of four students in a top law school in Manila's Makati financial district.

Ramos ordered national police chief Recaredo Sarmiento to seek the cooperation of the victims' parents and the officials of the school, who preferred to keep quiet about the incidents, a presidential palace statement said.
The students, kidnapped separately in recent weeks, have been released but requested anonymity, it said.
Although the school has not confirmed the incidents, some students have, saying they saw gunmen snatch two of the students from a parking area, the statement said.
The family of one of the students reportedly paid the kidnappers five million pesos ($175,000) but it was not known if the relatives of the others also paid ransoms, it said.

Kidnapping has become a flourishing business in the country with gangs collecting 152 million pesos in ransoms from families of 89 victims in the first four months of 1997, or more than what they collected for all of 1996, anti-crime groups said.
Widespread suspicion that police and soldiers are protecting the gangs has made families of victims reluctant to cooperate with the authorities.
